Performance evaluation in MEA systems reveals that sulfidation markedly enhances C 2 H 4 selectivity and partial current density (PCD). For spherical Cu electrodes, sulfidation to a S/Cu surface ratio of 0.33 resulted in a 1.76-fold increase in C 2 H 4 PCD, from 58.2 to 102.5 mA/cm 2 at 3.2 V. In situ Raman spectroscopy suggests that sulfur coordination stabilizes bridge-bonded CO and promotes the formation of the CH 2 CHO intermediate, which is consistent with the enhanced C 2 H 4 activity. Density functional theory calculations reveal that Cu-rich sulfide surfaces, including Cu 2 S and Cu 31 S 16 , stabilize *OCCO intermediates, suggesting a thermodynamically favorable C–C coupling reaction pathway through synergistic Cu–S coordination. These findings identify surface sulfur incorporation as a structural motif that actively promotes CO dimerization and enhances C 2 H 4 selectivity under MEA conditions.

title: An interstitial fluid-like NICHE-chip for neural stem cell niche modeling and nanoscale neurotrophic delivery
abstract: Neural stem cells (NSCs) reside in anatomically confined niches, where three-dimensional (3D) geometry and interstitial fluid (ISF) flow collectively regulate NSC behavior. However, in vitro platforms that simultaneously recapitulate size-controlled 3D architecture, ISF-like dynamics, and nanoscale therapeutic delivery remain limited. Here, we present a 3D printing-based platform with multi-sized microwells, termed the Neural-Inspired Culture for a Hydrodynamic Environment (NICHE)-chip, which incorporates an osmosis-driven flow system to generate ISF-like flow. The NICHE-chip enabled stable formation of uniform human neural stem cell (hNSC) neurospheres across defined microwell sizes. Under ISF-like flow, hNSC neurospheres showed enhanced viability, reduced apoptosis, and increased self-renewal and differentiation marker expression, particularly in 100 μm microwells. ISF-like flow also promoted laminin-rich extracellular matrix (ECM) deposition and cell-cell interactions, suggesting niche-like remodeling of the 3D microenvironment. In the ISF-integrated 100 μm neurosphere model, amyloid-β (Aβ) was introduced to establish an Alzheimer's disease (AD)-like neurotoxicity model, which was then used to evaluate nanoparticle-mediated neurotrophic factor delivery using brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF)-loaded poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) nanoparticles. BDNF-loaded PLGA nanoparticles (BDNF-NPs) enabled sustained BDNF delivery, attenuated Aβ-induced neuronal marker loss, and counter-regulated a subset of Aβ-induced transcriptional alterations associated with neuroprotection. Overall, the NICHE-chip provides an ISF-integrated 3D neurosphere culture platform for NSC niche modeling, AD-like neurotoxicity assessment, and nanoscale neurotrophic factor delivery.

title: Bias-programmable linear-to-nonlinear photoresponse for filter-free single-pixel VIS–NIR discrimination
abstract: Abstract Filter-free discrimination of visible (VIS) and near-infrared (NIR) light within a single photodetector pixel remains challenging because conventional photodiodes typically require optical filters or multiple detector elements. This work reports a monolithic nonlinear back-to-back photodiode (NL-BPD) that enables bias-programmable reconfiguration between high-linear-dynamic-range (LDR) photodetection and nonlinear spectral-discrimination modes. By changing the bias from − 0.5 V to + 0.5 V, the device's initially independent linear responses in both VIS and NIR channels (LDRs ≥ 100 dB) evolve into a nonlinear regime in which the VIS response reverses polarity with increasing light intensity while the NIR response remains monotonic. This behavior is enabled by defect-assisted transport pathways formed through partial interfacial reactions between the highly conductive PEDOT:PSS interlayer and MAPbI 3 . Together with the optimized device architecture, this interfacial current-path engineering reduces resistive bottlenecks and promotes cooperative carrier extraction from both absorbers. The resulting electrical signatures allow mixed VIS–NIR signals to be decoded from a single electrical output without optical filters or spatially separated pixels. The NL-BPD enables accurate spectral reconstruction (average R 2 = 0.9996), demonstrates single-point pulse oximetry, and achieves > 96% accuracy in normalized-difference-vegetation-index-based vegetation health classification. These results establish bias-programmable nonlinear photodetection as an effective strategy for single-pixel multispectral sensing.

title: Fluorine surface engineering for Vt control and memory window boost in HZO FeFET toward high-performance, energy-efficient in-memory computing
abstract: Threshold-voltage (Vt) control without sacrificing the memory window remains a key challenge for energy-efficient ferroelectric field-effect transistor (FeFET)-based in-memory computing. Here, we introduce a novel fluorine surface treatment (FST)-based Vt tuning strategy that selectively engineers the interfacial layer of Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 based Si FeFETs. Fluorine-induced electrostatic modulation and interfacial defect passivation jointly contribute to a positive shift of the entire transfer hysteresis and memory-window enhancement without noticeably altering the ferroelectric switching characteristics of the HZO layer. The optimized FST achieves an approximately 0.5 V positive Vt shift, an approximately 0.5 V memory window enhancement, and a 40× reduction in leakage current at 0 V, enabling normally-off operation of the low-Vt state. The resulting devices exhibit robust reliability, consistent device-to-device characteristics, and favorable analog synaptic behavior. Furthermore, simulation using the experimentally measured device characteristics improves CIFAR-10 classification accuracy from approximately 78% to 83%. These results establish interfacial-layer-selective fluorine engineering as a compelling route toward low-leakage, reliable, and energy-efficient FeFET-based analog in-memory computing.
